9. Red Marrow Branding and creative communications Startups and growing businesses
10. Serviceplan Middle East Integrated creative and marketing solutions Regional and international campaigns

1. Darwin Corp: Dubai-based global creative and digital experience agency

Location: Meydan Free Zone, Dubai, United Arab Emirates Service coverage: UAE and international markets through remote collaboration Specialisations: Creative direction, branding, interactive website development, UI/UX design, motion design and digital experiences Website: https://www.thedarwin.co/

As businesses compete through digital experiences and not traditional advertising alone, agencies that combine design, technology and strategic thinking are becoming more relevant. Darwin Corp describes itself as a motion-driven creative studio, based in Dubai and available worldwide.

The studio provides branding, design and digital development services to businesses in the UAE and international markets. It operates through a global collaboration model, so companies in other countries can use its creative capabilities remotely. The company says it has shaped more than 40 brands across 15 countries.

A creative approach beyond conventional website design

A company's website is often the first significant interaction between a brand and its potential customers. In competitive markets, that first impression can shape how customers judge credibility, professionalism and quality.

Darwin Corp approaches digital design through the relationship between visual storytelling, user experience and technology. Its websites and digital platforms are built to communicate brand identity while staying intuitive to use. The studio treats websites as experiences, using animation, interaction and considered design, and not as static collections of information. That approach is most relevant for businesses trying to stand out in crowded industries.

Core creative services

Brand identity and creative direction. Brand positioning, visual systems, logo design, typography, design direction and digital brand expression, aimed at giving businesses a distinctive visual identity.

Interactive website design and development. Central to the studio's work. It combines contemporary visual design, responsive layouts, custom development, including Webflow builds, and interactive elements for corporate websites and digital platforms.

UI/UX design. Interfaces that balance visual sophistication with clarity, usability and functionality, so customers can understand and use digital products.

Motion design and digital storytelling. Motion graphics, animation and interactive storytelling that help brands explain complex ideas. These are particularly useful for technology companies, premium brands and businesses seeking a distinctive digital identity.

Creative technology and AI-assisted experiences. AI art direction, generative AI and other emerging tools, integrated into digital production and visual experiences.

Serving businesses globally from Dubai

Although headquartered in Dubai, the studio works with businesses across different markets through remote collaboration. Companies in London, New York, Riyadh, Singapore or Sydney can engage a Dubai-based creative partner without needing an agency office in their own city.

Remote communication, digital project management and online collaboration allow cross-border projects to be developed and delivered. For international businesses, the model offers specialised creative capabilities with flexibility in how projects are managed. It also reflects a wider shift in creative services, where expertise and digital collaboration matter alongside physical location.

Who should consider Darwin Corp?

  • Startups developing a distinctive brand identity and professional digital presence.
  • Established businesses seeking premium website redesigns.
  • Technology companies requiring sophisticated digital storytelling.
  • Real estate, hospitality and luxury businesses investing in stronger digital presentation.
  • International companies looking for remote creative and development partners.
  • Organisations seeking integrated branding, UI/UX and interactive website development.

Why Darwin Corp is worth considering

The studio's combination of creative direction, design and technology makes it an option for businesses looking beyond conventional marketing deliverables. Its positioning is built around one line: "Don't make an ad. Make an experience." For businesses investing in their long-term digital presence, the approach emphasises meaningful design and memorable customer interactions.

Best for: Premium website development, interactive digital experiences, UI/UX design, brand identity and globally accessible creative services.

Explore Darwin Corp: https://www.thedarwin.co/

2. Impact BBDO: established creative advertising agency

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Creative advertising, brand campaigns, integrated communications and strategic storytelling Website: https://www.impactbbdo.com/

Impact BBDO is one of the established names in Dubai's advertising industry, with a longstanding presence in the Middle East. It is associated with large-scale creative campaigns and brand communications across regional and international markets.

Its work spans creative strategy, campaign development and integrated advertising, which suits organisations seeking broad consumer reach.

The agency was named Middle East & Africa Agency of the Year in The One Club for Creativity's 2025 Global Creative Rankings. At The One Show 2025 it also won the region's first Best of Show pencil.

Creative strengths

Impact BBDO's capabilities suit businesses that need campaign ideas that work across multiple channels. It does not focus exclusively on digital products or website development. It works within the broader advertising and brand communications landscape, developing concepts that extend across traditional media, digital advertising and integrated campaigns.

Who should consider Impact BBDO?

Large consumer brands, established corporations and organisations planning significant advertising initiatives may find its experience and creative network relevant.

Best for: High-profile advertising campaigns, brand communications and integrated creative strategy.

3. FP7 McCann: integrated advertising and brand communications

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Advertising, creative strategy, integrated campaigns and brand communications Website: https://www.fp7mccann.com/

FP7 McCann is a prominent advertising agency within the McCann network. Founded in 1968 and headquartered in Dubai, it works across brand strategy, creative advertising and integrated marketing communications.

Its regional experience makes it relevant for businesses seeking campaigns that connect with audiences across different cultural and commercial environments.

Creative strengths

FP7 McCann combines creative ideas with broader communications strategy. Its work suits organisations that need campaigns running across multiple platforms and markets.

In the 2025 Effie Index, FP7 McCann Dubai ranked first among agency offices in the Middle East and Africa, a measure of marketing effectiveness. The network also took 15 wins at the 2025 MENA Effie Awards, and the Dubai office collected seven Lions at Cannes Lions 2025.

Who should consider FP7 McCann?

Companies seeking integrated advertising capabilities, regional brand communications and campaign development may benefit from considering the agency.

Best for: Multinational brands, regional advertising campaigns and integrated marketing communications.

4. VML: creative technology, digital experiences and commerce

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Creative advertising, customer experience, digital transformation and commerce Website: https://www.vml.com/

VML is an international creative company with capabilities spanning brand creativity, technology, customer experience and commerce. Its Dubai presence connects businesses with a wider international network of creative and digital expertise.

Customer experiences now extend across websites, mobile platforms, digital services and commerce environments. Agencies working where creativity meets technology have become important partners for large organisations, and VML operates in this space.

Creative strengths

The agency's capabilities cover connected customer experiences, digital platforms and integrated creative services. For businesses managing complex digital ecosystems, this can help align creative communications with broader customer experience requirements.

At network level, VML entered the top five agency networks in the 2024 Effie Index.

Who should consider VML?

VML is particularly relevant for enterprise organisations, international businesses and companies undertaking complex digital transformation.

Best for: Enterprise digital experiences, connected commerce, creative technology and large-scale digital transformation.

5. Saatchi & Saatchi Middle East: creative advertising and brand storytelling

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Advertising, brand storytelling, creative campaigns and integrated communications Website: https://www.saatchi.ae/

Saatchi & Saatchi is one of the internationally recognised names in creative advertising. Its Middle Eastern operation, part of Publicis Groupe Middle East, contributes to Dubai's established advertising and communications industry.

The agency develops creative ideas that connect brands with consumers through storytelling, advertising and integrated communications.

Creative strengths

Saatchi & Saatchi Middle East suits businesses that need campaign-led creativity and broader brand communications. Its capabilities are geared to turning strategic brand objectives into advertising concepts that reach diverse audiences.

In the 2025 Loeries MENA agency rankings, it placed second. It ranked third across the combined Africa and Middle East region.

Who should consider Saatchi & Saatchi?

Businesses seeking an established advertising partner for consumer campaigns, brand storytelling and integrated communications may find the agency suitable.

Best for: Creative advertising, consumer campaigns and brand storytelling.

6. ASTUDIO: luxury branding and premium visual production

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Luxury creative services, photography, film, branding and digital content Website: https://astudio.ae/

Dubai's luxury economy has created significant demand for premium creative production. Luxury hospitality groups, real estate developers, fashion brands and lifestyle businesses often need visual content that reflects sophisticated brand positioning.

ASTUDIO operates in this segment. It describes itself as a boutique, full-service creative, digital and production agency, with its MENA headquarters in Dubai. Its work centres on high-end visual storytelling, including photography, film production, branding and digital content.

Creative strengths

ASTUDIO's capabilities suit businesses where visual presentation is central to the customer experience. Luxury brands often need consistency across advertising, photography, video and digital communications. A specialist production partner can help hold that visual direction across channels.

Who should consider ASTUDIO?

Luxury brands, premium hospitality businesses, real estate companies and lifestyle organisations seeking polished creative production may find ASTUDIO worth exploring.

Best for: Luxury branding, photography, film production and premium visual storytelling.

7. Yellow: brand strategy and creative identity

Location: Dubai Media City, Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Brand strategy, visual identity and creative communications Website: https://welcometoyellow.com/

Yellow is a Dubai-born branding and creative consultancy, founded in 2017. It helps businesses define their brand positioning and turn strategic ideas into distinctive visual identities. Its credits include naming and launching the on-demand fuel brand CAFU, according to a third-party agency listing.

In a market where businesses compete across many industries, branding helps organisations communicate their value. A strong identity system creates consistency across websites, packaging, marketing materials and customer interactions.

Creative strengths

Yellow's branding-focused approach suits organisations seeking strategic brand development, as opposed to a single advertising campaign. Its services apply most to businesses launching new brands, refreshing existing identities or entering competitive markets.

Who should consider Yellow?

Businesses requiring brand strategy, identity development and consistent creative communications may find Yellow a suitable partner.

Best for: Brand identity, brand strategy and creative positioning.

8. Skyne: strategic branding and brand transformation

Location: Dubai Design District, Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Strategic branding, brand identity and design consultancy Website: https://skyne.com/

Skyne is a strategic branding and design consultancy headquartered in Dubai, with offices in Riyadh, Muscat and Rotterdam. It focuses on connecting business objectives with brand strategy and design.

For established businesses, branding often involves more than a new visual identity. It can mean reconsidering how the organisation is positioned, how it communicates its value and how customers perceive its products or services. Skyne works within this discipline.

Creative strengths

The agency's approach suits businesses undertaking brand transformation, repositioning or broader identity development. Its strategic orientation fits organisations that want a structured branding process.

Who should consider Skyne?

Corporate organisations, growing businesses and companies planning significant brand development may find Skyne worth considering.

Best for: Corporate branding, strategic identity development and brand transformation.

9. Red Marrow: branding and creative communications

Location: Business Bay, Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Branding, brand strategy, identity design and creative communications Website: https://www.marrow.red

Red Marrow is a Dubai-based branding and creative agency, established in 2020, working across brand development and visual communications. Its services suit businesses seeking to establish or strengthen their identity in competitive markets.

For startups and growing companies, branding is a foundation for communicating professionalism and building recognition. A consistent brand system supports everything from website design and marketing materials to customer-facing communications.

Creative strengths

Red Marrow's focus on brand positioning, strategy and design makes it relevant to organisations that need a cohesive visual identity. It may appeal to businesses seeking a partner for brand development or repositioning.

Who should consider Red Marrow?

Startups, growing businesses and established companies seeking branding and creative communications services may find the agency worth exploring.

Best for: Brand development, visual identity and creative communications.

10. Serviceplan Middle East: integrated creative and marketing solutions

Location: Dubai, UAE Specialisations: Creative advertising, integrated marketing and brand communications Website: https://www.serviceplan.com/

Serviceplan Middle East is part of the international Serviceplan Group. It combines creative and strategic capabilities within a wider marketing and communications network.

For organisations operating across multiple markets, integrated creative services help coordinate campaigns and keep communication consistent across channels. Serviceplan is positioned in this segment.

Creative strengths

The agency's network lets it approach creative communications from an integrated perspective. Its work suits organisations that need coordinated brand campaigns and marketing initiatives.

Serviceplan Middle East ranked eighth in the 2025 Loeries MENA agency rankings and sixth in the Loeries independent agency ranking.

Who should consider Serviceplan?

International brands, established companies and organisations requiring integrated creative campaigns may find Serviceplan relevant.

Best for: Integrated creative campaigns, brand communications and regional marketing initiatives.

Creative agencies in Dubai: which type is right for your business?

The agencies above all operate within Dubai's creative industry, but their services are not identical. Understanding the differences helps businesses choose a partner.

Branding agencies

Branding agencies define how businesses present themselves to customers. Their work may include brand strategy, positioning, naming, visual identity, typography, packaging and brand guidelines. These services matter most to new businesses and companies undertaking a rebrand.

Advertising agencies

Advertising agencies communicate brand messages through campaigns. Their services can include campaign strategy, creative concepts, copywriting, advertising production and integrated communications. They often suit businesses seeking broader consumer awareness.

Digital creative agencies

Digital creative agencies combine design and technology to create websites, digital platforms and interactive experiences. Their capabilities may include UI/UX design, website development, motion graphics, digital storytelling and creative technology. For businesses investing in their online presence, these services can be particularly important.

Creative production studios

Creative production studios produce visual assets such as photography, film, animation and digital content. They are most relevant for businesses that depend heavily on visual presentation.

Why businesses in Dubai are investing in professional creative services

Dubai attracts businesses from many industries, including real estate, finance, technology, hospitality, retail and professional services. That diversity creates a competitive environment where companies must communicate their value clearly. A strong brand identity and professional digital presence help businesses differentiate themselves and build credibility.

First impressions influence customer perception

For many potential customers, the first interaction with a company happens online. A website's design, usability, content and overall presentation shape how visitors perceive the business.

Poor navigation, outdated design or unclear messaging make it harder for visitors to understand the company's services. A professionally developed website helps communicate expertise and guides users towards meaningful actions.

Digital experiences are becoming more important

As businesses invest in digital transformation, websites are expected to provide more than basic information. Interactive storytelling, purposeful motion, intuitive navigation and responsive interfaces all contribute to more engaging customer experiences.

Visual sophistication should never come at the expense of usability, accessibility or website performance. The strongest digital experiences balance creativity with practical functionality.

Brand consistency builds recognition

A business may communicate with customers through its website, social media, advertising, presentations, packaging and physical locations. Consistent visual identity and messaging help customers recognise the brand across these channels. Creative agencies play an important role in developing and maintaining that consistency.

Can Dubai creative agencies work with international clients?

Yes. A business does not need to be located in Dubai to work with a Dubai-based creative agency. Modern collaboration tools let agencies manage projects across countries and time zones.

Remote creative services can include brand strategy, visual identity development, UI/UX design, website development, motion graphics and digital production. For international companies, this gives access to specialist expertise without a local agency office.

Benefits of working with a remote creative agency

Access to international expertise. Businesses can choose partners on relevant capabilities and experience, not geographical proximity alone.

Flexible collaboration. Online meetings, shared project management platforms and digital review processes let teams work together across locations.

Consistent creative delivery. Remote workflows can support projects with multiple stakeholders, provided responsibilities, communication schedules and approval processes are clearly defined.

International business perspective. Agencies working with international clients may develop a broader understanding of different markets, customer expectations and digital communication requirements.

Dubai as a base for global creative services

Dubai's international business environment makes it a natural base for companies offering services beyond the UAE. Agencies in the city can collaborate with businesses in Europe, Asia, North America and other Middle Eastern markets.

Darwin Corp, for example, positions its Dubai-based studio as an internationally accessible creative partner. It offers remote collaboration for branding, website development, UI/UX and digital experience projects. For companies seeking a creative agency in Dubai with worldwide service capabilities, this is an alternative to choosing partners by local office location alone.

How much does it cost to hire a creative agency in Dubai?

Creative agency pricing in Dubai varies considerably with the scope of work, complexity, agency structure and required deliverables.

A small brand identity project involves a different level of investment from a large corporate rebrand. A basic informational website differs significantly from a custom-developed platform with complex functionality, integrations, animation and interactive experiences. Several factors influence pricing.

Project complexity

Projects involving custom development, extensive research, sophisticated animation or multiple deliverables generally require more resources.

Agency expertise

Established international networks, independent studios and specialist consultancies may use different pricing structures.

Scope and deliverables

The number of pages, design concepts, revisions, brand assets, technical integrations and production requirements all influence the overall budget.

Ongoing support

Some projects need maintenance, content updates, digital improvements or long-term creative collaboration after launch.

Businesses should not select an agency on the lowest quotation alone. They should evaluate the proposed deliverables, relevant experience, technical capabilities and expected business value. A detailed project brief helps agencies provide more accurate proposals.

How to choose the best creative agency in Dubai

Selecting the right agency requires a clear understanding of your business objectives. Before deciding, consider these questions.

1. What does your business actually need?

Determine whether your priority is brand identity, advertising, website development, digital transformation or content production.

An agency specialising in large-scale advertising campaigns may not be the ideal partner for a complex interactive website. A digital product studio may not be the best choice for a traditional television advertising campaign.

2. Does the agency have relevant experience?

Review the agency's portfolio and look for projects that demonstrate the capabilities you need. Consider the quality of the work, the challenges addressed and the role the agency played. Where possible, ask for measurable outcomes or client references.

3. Can the agency support your long-term goals?

A website, brand identity or digital platform may need to evolve as your business grows. Consider whether the agency can support future development, improvements and additional creative requirements.

4. Does the agency understand user experience?

For digital projects, visual appearance is only one part of the equation. Navigation, accessibility, responsiveness, performance and usability all influence the customer experience. Choose a digital partner that understands how design decisions affect real users.

5. How does the agency manage communication?

Clear communication is particularly important for complex or international projects. Discuss timelines, approval processes, responsibilities and communication expectations before beginning.

6. Is the agency transparent about deliverables?

A professional proposal should clearly define the scope of work, timeline, responsibilities, deliverables and commercial terms. This reduces misunderstandings and supports a more productive working relationship.

Final thoughts: choosing the right creative partner in Dubai

This section is analysis, not reporting.

Dubai's creative industry offers businesses a broad range of expertise, from internationally recognised advertising networks to independent digital studios and specialist branding consultancies. The right agency depends on the nature of the project.

Businesses planning large-scale advertising campaigns may benefit from established networks such as Impact BBDO, FP7 McCann or Saatchi & Saatchi. Companies undertaking enterprise digital transformation may find VML's broader technology and customer experience capabilities relevant. Luxury brands seeking high-end visual production may consider specialists such as ASTUDIO.

For businesses seeking a combination of brand identity, interactive website development, UI/UX design and motion-driven digital experiences, Darwin Corp offers a Dubai-based creative model accessible to clients internationally.

Choosing a creative agency should be about more than reputation or visual style. The most valuable partnerships rest on a shared understanding of business objectives, relevant expertise, transparent communication and the ability to turn ideas into meaningful outcomes.

As Dubai continues developing as an international business destination, agencies that combine creativity, technology and customer-focused design will remain important partners for businesses building stronger brands and digital experiences.

Parts of the UAE could see light rain from Monday 16 to Wednesday 18 November, after a partly cloudy weekend with strong winds and rough seas, according to the National Centre of Meteorology (NCM). Dubai is forecast to reach about 30°C on Saturday.

The rain is expected to be light and localised, not widespread, and the forecast does not name individual cities. This report reflects the NCM's five-day forecast as reported on 14 November, and forecasts are updated daily.

UAE weather today: Saturday 14 November

Saturday is partly cloudy to cloudy at times, with low clouds over the coast and islands. Winds are light to moderate, shifting from northwesterly to southwesterly at 10 to 25km/h and reaching up to 40km/h.

Rain forecast: Monday to Wednesday

Sunday 15 November. Partly cloudy, with low clouds forming over some areas, particularly along the coast and islands.

Monday 16 November. Partly cloudy to cloudy across the country. Light rain could fall over islands and some coastal and northern areas.

Tuesday 17 November. Similar conditions, with light rain again possible in the same areas.

Wednesday 18 November. The chance of light rain continues, with the five-day forecast pointing to some coastal, northern and eastern areas.

The NCM's forecast indicates rainfall will be limited to certain areas. Some places may see showers while nearby areas stay dry.

Strong winds and rough seas

The Arabian Gulf is forecast to be rough, becoming very rough at times in western areas. The Oman Sea is easing, although reports differ on whether Saturday's conditions there are moderate or still rough at times.

The NCM issued a marine advisory for sea-goers and fishermen covering 10 to 16 November. A separate warning for northwesterly winds of up to 45km/h and waves of up to 8ft runs until 8am on Sunday 15 November. Sea conditions in the Gulf are forecast to ease to rough-to-moderate on Monday.

Background: an unsettled week and El Niño

The weekend follows several days of unsettled weather. Showers were reported in parts of Sharjah on 11 November, including Mleiha, Al Madam and Al Badayer.

The NCM has also forecast a 96% probability that El Niño will persist from November 2026 to March 2027. It stressed that the figure refers to the phenomenon continuing, not to the chance of rain in the UAE. Its seasonal outlook suggests temperatures and rainfall could be near or above average over the period. El Niño's influence on the Gulf is indirect, working through wind patterns and the movement of low-pressure systems.

What residents should know

  • Motorists: rain can make roads slippery after dry spells. Reduce speed and keep a safe following distance.
  • Marine activities: strong winds and rough seas are hazardous. Follow official marine warnings before going out.
  • Outdoor plans: mild temperatures suit outdoor activities, but wind and occasional showers may affect some plans.
  • Mountain and desert trips: weather can change quickly. Avoid wadis during heavy rain or flash-flood warnings.

What to watch

  • The NCM's daily forecasts for where Monday's showers are most likely.
  • Whether the marine advisory is extended beyond 16 November.
  • Official updates at https://www.ncm.ae/.

Iran has launched a new wave of aerial attacks towards Bahrain, according to Bahraini and Iranian statements, escalating tensions across the Middle East as the conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel threatens to destabilise the Gulf.

On Sunday 15 November 2026, Bahrain's Defence Force announced that its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial threats targeting the kingdom. The announcement followed nationwide security warnings, with residents told to seek shelter as sirens sounded across parts of Bahrain.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed responsibility for launching six drones at a US air-defence radar installation at the Al-Riffa helicopter base. The reported destruction of the radar has not been independently verified, and neither Bahraini nor US authorities had confirmed that the alleged strike hit its target at the time of reporting.

The incident is another escalation in a regional conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February 2026.

What happened in Bahrain on 15 November?

Bahrain's Interior Ministry issued multiple security alerts early on Sunday morning, with the first reportedly around 4:30 a.m. local time, followed by another as authorities monitored the situation. Residents were advised to stay calm, move to secure locations and rely on official government communications.

The IRGC announced that it had targeted a US military radar installation with six drones. Bahrain's military then confirmed that its air defences had intercepted several incoming aerial attacks. The exact number of drones intercepted, whether any reached their targets and the extent of any damage were not immediately established. Unverified footage circulating online purportedly shows drones over Riffa, but its authenticity has not been confirmed.

Why is Iran targeting Bahrain?

Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, which plays a significant role in American operations across the Persian Gulf, the Arabian Sea and surrounding maritime routes. That military relationship makes Bahrain strategically important during any confrontation between Washington and Tehran.

Iran has repeatedly accused the United States of conducting military operations against Iranian infrastructure and has described its attacks on US-linked facilities as retaliation.

It was the second time in three days that the IRGC claimed to have targeted a US radar in Bahrain. On Friday 13 November, the IRGC said it had successfully attacked an American early-warning radar installation. US Central Command rejected the claim, saying American forces had intercepted two Iranian attack drones and that the incident caused no injuries or damage. Iran said its earlier operation was retaliation for what it described as an American strike on a telecommunications installation in Iran's southern Hormozgan province, a claim I could not independently verify.

The competing accounts show how difficult it is to verify battlefield claims during an active conflict.

Bahrain condemns Iranian attacks and calls for international action

Bahrain has strongly condemned the renewed attacks as violations of its sovereignty and threats to regional stability. It has called for international action and urged implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2817. Bahrain authored the resolution on behalf of the Gulf Cooperation Council states and Jordan. It was adopted by 13 votes to none, with China and Russia abstaining, and it condemns Iranian attacks and any Iranian action aimed at obstructing navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's UN envoy rejected it as a politically motivated abuse of the council's authority, per UN News.

The Arab Parliament also condemned Sunday's drone attacks and expressed solidarity with Bahrain, stressing the importance of protecting the sovereignty and security of Gulf states. The diplomatic response reflects growing concern that military exchanges involving US facilities in Gulf countries could expose neighbouring states to further attacks.

Could the Iran-Bahrain conflict spread across the Gulf?

The latest developments have raised concerns about wider escalation. Bahrain is not the only country facing security threats. On 15 November, the Saudi-led coalition reportedly intercepted two ballistic missiles heading towards Riyadh and three drones in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. Those incidents were associated with the separate conflict involving Yemen's Houthi movement and were not confirmed as direct Iranian attacks. I could not independently verify these reports.

The broader security environment remains fragile. Military activity near major shipping routes, attacks on infrastructure and uncertainty over diplomatic negotiations have raised the risk of further confrontation. A particularly sensitive location is the Strait of Hormuz, through which a large share of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supply normally passes.

Strait of Hormuz: why the conflict matters to global oil markets

The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to international shipping routes through the Gulf of Oman. Disruption there can have major consequences for global energy markets. Before the conflict it carried about a fifth of the world's oil. UN News, citing UK Maritime Trade Operations, reports that transits are around 65% below pre-conflict levels and that October saw the most incidents since the war began.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed that two oil tankers struck naval mines while attempting to transit the strait on 14 November, and maritime authorities reportedly described an attack involving a tanker sailing towards the strait on Sunday. The details of these incidents were not independently established in the initial reports, and I could not verify them.

Prolonged instability could contribute to:

  • Higher shipping and maritime insurance costs.
  • Volatility in international oil and natural gas prices.
  • Disruption to cargo movements and supply chains.
  • Higher operating costs for businesses relying on Gulf shipping routes.
  • Greater uncertainty for regional tourism, aviation and investment.

The scale of any economic impact would depend on how long the disruption continues and whether military activity intensifies.

What does the attack mean for the UAE and other Gulf countries?

The UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain are closely connected through regional trade, aviation, energy markets and security relationships. A prolonged confrontation could affect business confidence and cross-border operations across the Gulf Cooperation Council region.

For the UAE, the potential consequences include changes to regional flight schedules, higher logistics costs and uncertainty over international trade. Some UAE airlines were reported to have adjusted selected Saudi routes amid security developments on 15 November, a report I could not verify.

These developments do not mean that every Gulf country faces the same threat or that the whole region is equally disrupted. Businesses and travellers should distinguish between verified government advisories and unconfirmed reports on social media.

US-Iran relations: a conflict with no clear resolution

The renewed attacks come amid stalled diplomatic efforts to end the conflict between Washington and Tehran. The war began in February 2026, when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran. Iran subsequently retaliated against US-linked military facilities across the Gulf and attempted to restrict maritime activity through the Strait of Hormuz.

Although the intensity of fighting has fluctuated, the underlying confrontation remains unresolved. US President Donald Trump has reportedly indicated that further military action remains possible if Iran threatens American forces or regional allies, and Iran has said it will respond to attacks on its territory and infrastructure. I could not verify those specific statements. These positions create a difficult diplomatic environment in which single military incidents could trigger further retaliation.

What happens next?

The situation remains unpredictable. Developments to watch include:

  • Military response: whether American or Bahraini authorities confirm damage from Sunday's reported drone operation, which could shape later military decisions.
  • Regional diplomacy: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is reportedly expected to visit Oman on Tuesday 17 November for talks with his Omani counterpart, according to Iranian state media (unverified). Oman has often served as a diplomatic channel in regional disputes.
  • Maritime security: continued incidents near the Strait of Hormuz could increase pressure on governments to strengthen shipping protection.
  • Civilian safety: Bahrain's authorities may issue further security instructions as events develop.

For now, the priority remains preventing further casualties, protecting civilian infrastructure and avoiding a wider regional confrontation.

Conclusion: Iran's Bahrain attacks highlight growing regional risks

Iran's latest drone operations towards Bahrain are a significant escalation in an already volatile conflict. Bahrain has confirmed intercepting several aerial threats, but Iran's claim that it struck American radar infrastructure remains unverified.

The attacks show how the confrontation between Iran and the United States can extend beyond their own territories and affect neighbouring Gulf states. With military activity continuing around strategic installations and major shipping routes, the consequences could reach international energy markets, aviation, trade and investor confidence. Whether the latest incident leads to further retaliation or renewed diplomatic engagement will be a crucial question in the days ahead.

This is a developing story. Military claims, casualty figures and damage assessments will be updated as verified information becomes available.

After years of speculation, the search for the next James Bond is over. Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as 007, succeeding Daniel Craig in one of cinema's most iconic roles.

Amazon MGM Studios confirmed the news on 16 November 2026, announcing that the British actor will lead the next instalment of the long-running spy franchise.

The film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, the filmmaker behind Dune, Blade Runner 2049 and Arrival, from a screenplay by Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight. The announcement marks a turning point for Bond, introducing a new leading man and a new creative direction under Amazon MGM Studios.

Robert Pattinson confirmed as the next James Bond

Pattinson, 40, becomes the seventh actor to play James Bond in the official film series, following Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig. His casting ends a long search for Craig's successor after the actor's final appearance in No Time to Die in 2021.

In the official announcement, Pattinson called the opportunity "the honour of a lifetime". He also thanked Villeneuve, the producers and the Amazon MGM team and described the role as a dream come true.

For audiences who have followed Pattinson's career, the casting is another striking turn for an actor who has repeatedly defied expectations.

Why Robert Pattinson was chosen

Pattinson's career has changed dramatically since his breakthrough as Edward Cullen in the Twilight franchise. Rather than staying in mainstream blockbusters, he took unconventional roles in independent films, showing versatility and a willingness to take creative risks.

His performances in Good Time, The Lighthouse and The Batman established him as an actor who can play complicated, emotionally intense characters. His recent work includes Mickey 17, Die, My Love, The Drama, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey and the thriller Primetime, with a role in Dune: Part Three, again for Villeneuve, due later this year.

That range could suit a modern take on James Bond. The character has evolved over six decades, from the sophisticated charm of Sean Connery's portrayal to the more physical and emotionally vulnerable version played by Daniel Craig. Pattinson could add another dimension: a Bond defined by intelligence, unpredictability, psychological complexity and understated charisma.

Amazon's own statement points the same way. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, cited Pattinson's range, screen presence and "quiet intensity", and the producers praised his fearlessness and self-deprecating wit.

Denis Villeneuve will direct the next Bond film

One of the most exciting parts of the announcement is Denis Villeneuve's involvement. The Canadian filmmaker has built a reputation for visually ambitious storytelling, atmospheric cinematography and complex characters. Blade Runner 2049, Arrival and the Dune films show his ability to combine large-scale spectacle with thoughtful, character-driven stories.

With Villeneuve directing, the next Bond film could take a more atmospheric and psychologically sophisticated direction. The screenplay is by Steven Knight, best known for creating Peaky Blinders, whose hiring was announced in August 2025. The pairing of Villeneuve's visual style, Knight's writing and Pattinson's acting has generated considerable anticipation.

Amazon MGM Studios begins a new era for 007

The casting is also a milestone for Amazon MGM Studios. In March 2025, Amazon MGM closed a joint venture with Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson under which the studio gains creative control of the James Bond rights. The upcoming film is the first Bond production developed under this new arrangement.

Amy Pascal and David Heyman are producing, through Pascal Pictures and Heyday Films, with Tanya Lapointe as executive producer. For Amazon MGM the stakes are high. Bond is among the most recognisable entertainment franchises in the world, with decades of cinematic history and a passionate international audience. The challenge is to preserve what made Bond iconic while introducing a version of the character that resonates with a new generation.

Who else was considered for James Bond?

Before Pattinson's confirmation, several British actors were linked to the role in media reports. Among the reported contenders were:

  • Aaron Taylor-Johnson
  • Callum Turner
  • Jack Lowden
  • Josh O'Connor
  • Henry Cavill
  • Theo James

Pattinson reportedly took part in screen tests in the final stages of casting, though this has not been confirmed by the studio. Villeneuve thanked the other actors who took part in the process. Although several names drew attention, Amazon MGM ultimately chose Pattinson to lead the franchise into its next era.

Will Robert Pattinson still play Batman?

Pattinson's casting raises an obvious question about his future as Bruce Wayne. He starred in Matt Reeves' The Batman, bringing a darker, more introspective take on the DC hero, and Amazon's announcement notes that he is currently in production on The Batman Part II.

With Pattinson now attached to two internationally recognised characters, audiences will be curious how the studios manage his commitments. His Bond casting does not itself confirm that he is leaving the Batman franchise, and further details on scheduling will depend on announcements from the studios involved.

When will the next James Bond movie be released?

Amazon MGM Studios has not announced a release date for Pattinson's first Bond film. The production is widely referred to as Bond 26, an informal label, and no official title has been revealed. Reports have suggested a possible 2028 theatrical release, but that should be treated as provisional until the studio confirms it. Further casting announcements, production details and the official title are expected as development progresses.

What Robert Pattinson could bring to James Bond

The casting suggests Amazon MGM is willing to take a distinctive creative direction. Unlike some traditional Bond candidates, Pattinson has built much of his reputation on unconventional performances. His ability to portray vulnerability, intensity and ambiguity could bring a different emotional dimension to 007.

Paired with Villeneuve's filmmaking, the next Bond film has the potential to combine the franchise's signature action, espionage and sophistication with a more contemporary cinematic identity. Ultimately, the success of Pattinson's interpretation will depend on how the film balances innovation with the traditions audiences associate with Bond.

A new James Bond era begins

Robert Pattinson's appointment is one of the most significant entertainment announcements of 2026. With Villeneuve directing, Knight writing and Amazon MGM Studios overseeing the franchise's next chapter, the creative team has considerable potential.

Pattinson now faces the challenge of following Daniel Craig's acclaimed interpretation while establishing his own identity as the world's most famous fictional secret agent. The name's Pattinson. Robert Pattinson. And the next era of James Bond has officially begun.
